- Use the assumptions and notation of Proposition 1.
- Let \(T=f_#\llbracket R\rrbracket\).

There is an integer \(m\in\mathbb Z\) such that
\[
T=m\llbracket S\rrbracket.
\]
fixed_proof:
By the constancy theorem on the connected open set \(\operatorname{int}S\),
\[
T\llcorner \operatorname{int}S
=
m\,\llbracket \operatorname{int}S\rrbracket
\]
for some \(m\in\mathbb Z\). Therefore \(T-m\llbracket S\rrbracket\) is supported in \(\partial S\). Since \(\partial S\) has \(\mathcal H^4\)-measure zero, no nonzero integral \(4\)-current can be supported there, so \(T=m\llbracket S\rrbracket\).
